key_insight: Extract Q-value estimates from a behavior cloning (BC) policy and use them to gate and guide online reinforcement learning, enabling safe, sample-efficient on-robot improvement without overwriting good demonstrated behaviors.
problem_solved: BC provides strong initial robot behavior but lacks a self-guided mechanism for online improvement; naive offline-to-online RL can overwrite demonstrated good actions due to distribution mismatch, harming safety and performance.
method: Train a Behavior Cloning policy on demonstration data and derive Q-value estimates from that BC policy (Q-Estimation).
Use those Q-estimates to build a Q-Gating mechanism that restricts or prioritizes online policy updates so only beneficial changes replace demonstrated actions.
Run lightweight on-robot RL guided by Q-gates to safely fine-tune behavior with few online samples and reduced catastrophic overwrite of demonstrations.
impact: Enables robots to continue learning on-device safely and efficiently after demonstrations, preserving high-quality demonstrated actions while improving performance with minimal online data — lowering deployment risk and sample cost for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Demonstrations -> Behavior Cloning -> Q-Estimation -> Q-Gating -> On-robot RL
Before/After chart: performance and safety metrics showing BC-only vs naive RL vs Q2RL (higher improvement + preserved safety)
Schematic of Q-Gating: action proposals filtered by BC-derived Q-thresholds (allow / block / prioritize updates)
Robot icon with sample-efficiency meter (few online steps) and shield icon representing preserved safe demo behaviors
paper_title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Lakshita Dodeja, Ondrej Biza, Shivam Vats, Stephen Hart, Stefanie Tellex
